walkthroughs.body_html:
Database Concepts — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Database Concepts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Database Concepts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

The first field of every table
A password protecting the database

mcqs.q: A range check is an example of:
options: Validation
Encryption
Compression
Defragmentation

mcqs.q: In a database table, a record is:
options: One row holding all the data about one entity instance
One column of the table
The table's title
A backup copy of the table

mcqs.q: The purpose of a primary key is to:
options: Uniquely identify each record in the table
Sort the table alphabetically
Encrypt sensitive fields
Count the number of fields

mcqs.q: Does validation prove that entered data is correct?
options: No - validation only checks data is sensible and allowed (right type, range or format); a wrong birthday can still pass if it is a valid date.
Yes - validation compares every entry with the real world.
Yes - data that passes validation must be accurate and true.
Yes - primary keys repeat once the table has many records.

mcqs.q: Can a primary key value appear in more than one record of its table?
options: Yes - primary keys repeat once the table has many records.
Yes - duplicates are fine if the other fields are different.
Yes - validation compares every entry with the real world.
No - the whole point of a primary key is uniqueness; duplicate key values would make records impossible to identify reliably.

mcqs.q: Are a field and a record the same thing?
options: No - a field is one column (a single category of data), while a record is one row (all the data about one entity instance).
A field is a row and a record is a column.
Yes - validation compares every entry with the real world.
Yes - field and record are interchangeable database words.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Validation”?
options: A field, or combination of fields, that uniquely identifies each record in a table, such as a StudentID.
Automatic checks applied when data is entered, such as range, length, format or presence checks, to ensure the data is sensible and allowed.
A real-world thing about which data is stored in a database, such as a student, product or appointment; each entity becomes a table.
A single item of data about an entity, forming one column of a table, such as Surname or DateOfBirth.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Record”?
options: One complete set of fields about a single entity instance, forming one row of a table.
A single item of data about an entity, forming one column of a table, such as Surname or DateOfBirth.
A field in one table that stores the primary key value of a record in another table, creating a link between the two tables.
A real-world thing about which data is stored in a database, such as a student, product or appointment; each entity becomes a table.

options: A field, or combination of fields, that uniquely identifies each record in a table, such as a StudentID.

One complete set of fields about a single entity instance, forming one row of a table.
